---
applyTo: "backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/**"
---

# Flyway migrations

- Migrations are **immutable** once committed: never edit, rename, reorder or delete an existing `V*.sql` file. Fix
  mistakes with a new migration.
- Name new files `V<next number>__<module>_<short_change>.sql` (e.g. `V7__forecasting_forecast_runs.sql`). Check the
  highest existing version first.
- Start with a comment naming the owning module. One module owns each table; document any cross-module foreign key
  and why it is acceptable.
- Types: `UUID` primary keys (generated by the application, UUIDv7), `TIMESTAMPTZ` for instants, `DATE` for trading
  days, `NUMERIC(19,6)` for prices and money (never floating point), `VARCHAR(n)` plus `CHECK` constraints instead of
  `CHAR(n)` (Hibernate validation rejects `bpchar` for `String`), `BIGINT version NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` on JPA
  aggregates.
- Add indexes for every query path (owner lookups, foreign keys used in joins, time ranges) and constraints that
  enforce invariants (uniqueness, normalisation, enumerations).
- Time series use natural composite keys, e.g. `PRIMARY KEY (stock_id, bar_date)`, so upserts are idempotent.
- Hibernate runs with `ddl-auto: validate`: the matching entity mapping must agree exactly (column names, types,
  lengths). Run `./mvnw verify` because integration tests apply all migrations to PostgreSQL 18.
- Seed data only for reference data (e.g. the stock catalogue), never for users or secrets.
